chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Yusuf ibn Aqil from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a man who ate a sheep along with some companions of his. He said, 'If you ate it, it is yours; and if you did not eat it, you are liable for such and such.' Then he ruled regarding it, 'That is invalid; there is no compensation (gharamah) for eating in food, whether little of it or much,' and he exempted them from paying the penalty for it.

key_terms.مَا قَلَّ مِنْهُ وَمَا كَثُرَ: Whether little of it or much

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on financial compensation for consuming food?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled a man and his companions who ate a sheep were not liable for a fixed financial penalty (gharamah), establishing that consumption of food does not incur a specific compensation regardless of quantity. This ruling highlights the distinction between *gharamah* (a fixed fine or penalty) and *daman* (liability for value), emphasizing that mere consumption does not automatically trigger a fixed monetary fine unless specified by custom or contract. The narration underscores the precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding the nature of financial liabilities in cases of usufruct or consumption.
